sources.entry: edgartools - Downloads SEC EDGAR filings and XBRL financial statements as structured data.

summary.one_liner: EdgarTools is a Python library that turns SEC EDGAR filings into typed Python objects and DataFrames, covering financial statements, insider trades, 13F holdings, fund portfolios and other filing types.
summary.what_it_does: It fetches SEC EDGAR filings and exposes them through one Python API, with standardized income statement, balance sheet and cash flow rows across companies, plus quarterly and trailing-twelve-month figures derived from XBRL. It parses 13F holdings, Form 4 insider transactions, N-PORT fund portfolios and 8-K items into typed objects and DataFrames. It extracts section text (for example Item 1A or Item 7) and whole filings as markdown for RAG use. It also provides full-text search over filing content since 2001, filing lookup by accession number, CIK or ticker, and access to the live filing feed. The README says it handles rate limiting, caching and offline storage, and that it keeps to the SEC's 10-requests-per-second fair-access limit.
use_cases: pull standardized financial statements for public companies
compare one metric like revenue across many companies
track insider buys and sells from Form 4 filings
build a RAG corpus from 10-K and 10-Q filings as markdown
search SEC filing text for keywords or 8-K item numbers
how_to_run: uv add edgartools  (or: pip install edgartools)
notable: Standardized statement rows that line up across filers, so the same label means the same metric for different companies
Typed parsers for 13F, Form 4, N-PORT and 8-K filings instead of raw XML
Full-text search over filing content since 2001, not just metadata
Optional local MCP server and agent skill for AI assistants, in the ai extra
caveats: Requires a contact email passed to the SEC on every request via set_identity; the README notes no API key is needed
SEC's fair-access limit of 10 requests per second applies
A hosted edgar.tools platform is offered separately and is paid for ongoing maintenance and cited answers; the library itself is free
